title: Reading in the digital age
text: Sales of printed books have been rising for several years, {{1}} surprised many in the publishing industry. E-books were supposed {{2}} replace paper entirely; instead, the two now coexist. Readers explain that paper suits long, concentrated reading, {{3}} screens are convenient for quick reference. Studies back this up: comprehension of complex texts is measurably better {{4}} paper. There is also the question of memory. Many readers remember {{5}} they have read a physical book, including {{6}} a key passage appeared. Psychologists suspect that the physical experience of a book — its weight and shape — provides {{7}} cues. Whatever the reason, few readers now argue that one format must {{8}} the other. Paper, it turns out, is technology too.

gaps.explanation: Sentential 'which' refers to the rising sales.
'where' = in which place (metaphorically, in the book).
'memory cues' — compound noun; spatial memory aids recall.
